clue.text: Don returned to empty well first

indicators.note: first tells us the well piece goes at the front

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring or well

indicators.note: returned means the word for empty is read backwards

parts.note: to drain is to empty

explanation.surface: A don comes back to drain a well before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns DRAIN into NIARD, which follows SPA. 'Don' is the Spanish title, not a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Don is a Spanish gentleman's title, so a don is a man from Spain.

clue.text: Money I'm wrong to put up — I'm a clown!

parts.note: P, a penny, is a small amount of money
if I'm wrong, I err: I + ERR

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word to is written bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone confesses a money mistake and declares themselves a clown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns TO into OT at the foot of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the sad white-faced clown of French pantomime.

clue.text: Ninety not put into cipher

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new form, rearranged

explanation.surface: Ninety is not to be encoded in a cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put into' signals the letters of NINETY NOT rearranged; 'cipher' is the person of no account, not a code.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher in the figurative sense is a person of no importance or influence.

clue.text: A spring swarm

parts.note: to bound is to leap or spring

explanation.surface: A spring swarm of insects.
explanation.definitionFit: To abound is to be present in great numbers, to teem.

clue.text: A future local government officer persuaded to do a U-turn

definitions.text: A future local government officer persuaded to do a U-turn

parts.words: A future local government officer persuaded to do a U-turn
parts.note: the legend of a poor boy leaving London who heard Bow bells say 'Turn again' and went back to become Lord Mayor

explanation.walkthrough: The Lord Mayor of London is the local government officer; in the pantomime story the bells persuade the boy to turn back.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk hero turned back on Highgate Hill and later served as Lord Mayor of London.

clue.text: Blow the meal!

explanation.definitionFit: To buffet is to strike repeatedly, and a buffet is a self-service spread of food.

clue.text: It proves which shell is fastest

definitions.text: It proves which shell is fastest

parts.words: It proves which shell is fastest
parts.note: a shell is a light racing rowing hull, so a contest between such craft decides the fastest

explanation.walkthrough: The annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing contest on the Thames is the famous one.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing contest decides which racing shell is quickest.

clue.text: Fellow bolted, went with the crowd

parts.note: a bolted door is locked

explanation.surface: A man locked his door and then followed the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolted' suggests running off, but it means fastened.
explanation.definitionFit: Flocked means gathered in a herd, moving along with everyone else.

clue.text: I'll make way for property in this country

indicators.note: make way for says the letter I steps aside for the property piece

parts.note: an estate is landed property

explanation.surface: A newcomer promises to clear space for real estate in their nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The I of 'I'll' is replaced inside THIS by ESTATE: TH-ESTATE-S.
explanation.definitionFit: The States is the everyday name for the United States of America, a nation.

clue.text: Slowly circling a building

indicators.note: circling means the word for slowly goes round the a

parts.note: lento is the musical direction for slowly

explanation.surface: Someone slowly walks round a building.
explanation.walkthrough: LENTO is the Italian tempo marking used in music.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a shed or extension built against a wall.

clue.text: Calmer, you cut short waving weapon

indicators.note: waving suggests the letters are swung about into a new order
cut short means the last letter of you is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone is told to calm down and stop brandishing a sword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' leaves YO; 'waving' mixes CALMER with YO.
explanation.definitionFit: A claymore is a large two-edged Scottish sword.

clue.text: Mint Ibsen's hero was said to be acquainted with

parts.note: Brand is the title character of an Ibsen verse play

indicators.note: was said means the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to have been acquainted with someone is to have known them

explanation.surface: A fresh Ibsen character was reportedly a friend of someone.
explanation.walkthrough: KNEW is heard as NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint condition means unused, as fresh as when made.

clue.text: Illegal ploy used by receiver in court

explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a criminal scheme, and also the strung bat a tennis player returning serve holds.

clue.text: Good and bad men joined band

parts.note: ST, a saint, is a good man
a rip is a dissolute rogue, a bad man

explanation.surface: Good men and bad men together formed a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a group of men, but it is a narrow piece of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip is a narrow length of material, like a ribbon.

clue.text: Ingredient of gunpowder, and Paris-style plaster perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be put in another order

parts.note: et is French for and

explanation.surface: Gunpowder and plaster of Paris are listed as ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' mixes ET with PLASTER; 'Paris-style plaster' looks like plaster of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is the oxidiser in black powder.

clue.text: Cast doubt upon record — Communist gets it

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
red is the colour and nickname of communists

explanation.surface: A Communist gets the blame for doubting the record.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit is to make something seem untrustworthy or false.

clue.text: The registration of Henry Holmes Unlimited with National Trust

indicators.note: unlimited means both names lose their first and last letters

parts.note: NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A man called Henry Holmes registers his company with the National Trust.
explanation.walkthrough: ENR and OLME come from Henry and Holmes without their ends; 'Unlimited' looks like a company name.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolment is the act of signing up or being entered on a register.

clue.text: A chap embraces another from 8

indicators.note: embraces means the word for chap holds the other name inside

parts.note: a chap is a man
another chap, Eric being a man's name

explanation.surface: A man hugs a friend who has come from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is the answer to 8 down, the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the USA is an American.

clue.text: Female forger was relieved

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a place, the town whose siege was lifted

parts.note: a lady is a woman
a smith forges metal at a forge

explanation.surface: A woman counterfeiter felt relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forger' suggests a counterfeiter but is a metalworker. Ladysmith in South Africa was besieged in the Boer War and famously relieved in 1900.
explanation.definitionFit: The South African town held out under Boer siege until British forces lifted it in 1900.

clue.text: Gargled messily, to get wet and dirty

indicators.note: messily says the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone gargled sloppily and got themselves soaked and grubby.
explanation.definitionFit: To draggle is to make clothing wet and muddy by trailing it.

clue.text: A sign of the times

parts.note: the symbol for multiplication, read as times in arithmetic

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means a typical feature of an era; here times means multiplied by.
explanation.definitionFit: The x-shaped multiplication symbol is a cross.

clue.text: Cadges cakes

explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to scrounge from others, and sponges are light airy cakes.

clue.text: Maintenance of Castle Rising?

parts.note: rising suggests up
a keep is the main tower of a castle

explanation.surface: A question about looking after Castle Rising.
explanation.walkthrough: Castle Rising is a real Norman castle in Norfolk, England. In this down clue UP sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the cost or work of keeping something in good repair.

clue.text: Song held in by musician

indicators.note: held in means the song is put inside the word for by

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A tune is kept to themselves by a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'musician' looks like the container but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone who performs on an instrument.

clue.text: A rod held by no Roman emperor

indicators.note: held by means the a-and-rod piece sits inside the Latin word

parts.note: non is Latin for not, so the Roman's no
a pole is a rod

explanation.surface: A rod is held by no Roman emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman emperor' looks like a single phrase, but 'Roman' belongs with 'no'.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French.

clue.text: Seen from behind, silent man-eating carnivore

indicators.note: seen from behind means the whole assembly is read in reverse
eating means the word for silent swallows the man

parts.note: tacit means unspoken, silent
Reg is a man's name

explanation.surface: A wild cat stalks quietly, eating people, from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: TACIT around REG makes TACREGIT; 'Seen from behind' turns all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger-cat is a small striped wild cat, a meat-eater.

clue.text: Come out and return, for example, with soldiers

indicators.note: return means the pieces that follow are read backwards

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Someone comes out and goes back with a troop of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns EGREME into EMERGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to appear or come into view.

clue.text: Still behind the Spanish team

indicators.note: behind means this piece follows the Spanish word

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
even, as in even more, means still

explanation.surface: A Spanish football side is still trailing.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has this many players.

clue.text: Simpleton loses heart, upset by unfair allocation of jobs

indicators.note: upset by means the remaining letters are knocked into a new order
loses heart means the middle letter of simpleton is dropped

explanation.surface: A fool is upset by unfair hiring.
explanation.walkthrough: SIMPLETON's centre letter L goes, and SIMPETON is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouritism to relatives when giving out posts.
